verified_identity: David A. Kelly, Hana Chockler, Daniel Kroening, Nathan Blake, Aditi Ramaswamy, Melane Navaratnarajah, and Aaditya Shivakumar; arXiv:2311.14081v1 (2023), DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2311.14081.
relevance_class: Method-adjacent: causal sufficient-pixel explanations for image object detectors; not image-forgery detection.
scope_and_methods: Full arXiv HTML read (abstract, method, experiments, conclusion, references). ANON-ReX adapts ReX/causal responsibility to multiple object detections, returning a pixel subset inside each detector box that preserves the original label under masking. Evaluates YOLOv8n, SSD, and Faster R-CNN on ImageNet-mini; excludes 210/3923 images with no YOLO detections. Compares query count and explanation size with a ReX baseline and analyzes two YOLO misclassifications.
observed_reliability_evidence: The explanation definition imposes model-internal sufficiency under a specified masking intervention and can expose plausible shortcut cues in two misclassification examples. Against the baseline, ANON-ReX uses fewer queries but produces explanations 20.7% larger for YOLO, 22.4% larger for SSD, and 52.9% larger for Faster R-CNN. The paper notes explanations may not be smallest and can inherit bounding-box geometry.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: No image-forgery/authenticity task, no independent ground-truth causal evidence map, and no explanation robustness, randomization, human agreement, or user reliance test. Preserving a label under masking is model-internal sufficiency, not proof that highlighted pixels are the authentic forensic evidence. The accuracy/meaning of masking and causal-independence assumptions remain intervention-dependent.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a lower-ranked image-explanation method neighbor for causal sufficiency and forensic-localization benchmark design; do not count it as direct forensic reliability evidence.

paper: Multiple Different Black Box Explanations for Image Classifiers
verified_identity: Hana Chockler, David A. Kelly, and Daniel Kroening; arXiv:2309.14309v4 (2025) and ECAI 2025 proceedings, first published online 2026-08-25, DOI 10.3233/FAIA250869. The 2023 arXiv title/version and formal proceedings record share authors and core method; treated as one research work pending line-by-line version comparison.
relevance_class: Method-adjacent: causal sufficiency, multiple explanations, and explanation-induced error discovery for image classifiers; not forensic detection.
scope_and_methods: Read the full arXiv HTML and official ECAI proceedings page. MultiReX uses approximate causal-responsibility ranking and a stochastic spatial search to find multiple minimal pixel subsets that alone retain the top class; compares explanation count, label position, and area against SAG on ImageNet-mini, VOC2012, and ECSSD using ResNet50, ConvNeXt-Large, and ViT-B/32. Includes a tennis-racket/shorts shortcut example and a preliminary occlusion example.
observed_reliability_evidence: MultiReX constrains explanations to the model's top class and reports smaller average explanations (~8% of image area vs ~14% for SAG at threshold 0.9); it exposes a region of a player's shorts that supports a tennis-racket label. SAG's explanations can fall far below the top class as its threshold changes. These are useful internal-consistency and shortcut-diagnostic results.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: No forensic/authenticity task or independent ground-truth causal evidence. Explanation count, area, and top-label preservation are not factual correctness or causal-faithfulness ground truth. The paper reports no user study of MultiReX, expert agreement, explanation randomization/robustness, or appropriate-reliance experiment. The authors acknowledge spatial search can miss non-contiguous explanations and did not comprehensively test occluded images. Comparison to SAG is not perfectly matched because the explanation definitions differ.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a high-value image-XAI method neighbor for explanation ambiguity and sufficiency controls, but do not count as direct forensic reliability evidence. Formal and arXiv versions are one work, not independent replication.

verified_identity: Hana Chockler, Daniel Kroening, and Youcheng Sun; IEEE/CVF ICCV 2021, pp. 1234–1243, DOI 10.1109/ICCV48922.2021.00127; arXiv:2103.03622.
relevance_class: Method-adjacent: causal sufficiency and evidence-grounding measures for explanations under occlusion; not image-forgery detection.
scope_and_methods: Full paper and official ICCV/arXiv records reviewed. DC-Causal uses causal responsibility to rank pixels and greedily construct a minimal subset that preserves the classifier label under masking. Evaluations include known-occlusion image sets, a Photo Bombing dataset with planted occlusion ground truth, and a non-occluded Roaming Panda set; comparison measures explanation size, overlap with planted occlusion, and IoU with the panda region. On COCO images without explanation ground truth, normalized size is only a proxy.
observed_reliability_evidence: On Photo Bombing, over 60% of DC-Causal explanations have no overlap with the planted occluder, which the paper reports as about 20% better than the next method (RISE); it also produces smaller explanations, but the size and occlusion-overlap rankings do not always agree. On Roaming Panda, overlap with the known panda region provides a separate localization check. The paper reports that varying mask color changes occlusion-overlap performance by less than 4% in its tested setup.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: This is not a forensic authenticity task. A planted occluder or panda mask is a useful localization reference, but it does not define the causal evidence needed to decide image authenticity. COCO evaluation lacks an explanation truth map and substitutes explanation size. The greedy explanation is an approximation; masking color and intervention distribution remain consequential, and stability across model/data shifts or human forensic judgments is not established.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a high-value image-domain method neighbor for evidence-overlap, sufficiency, and multi-metric evaluation design. Do not count it as direct forensic explanation-reliability evidence.

paper: One Explanation is Not Enough: Structured Attention Graphs for Image Classification
verified_identity: Vivswan Shitole, Fuxin Li, Minsuk Kahng, Prasad Tadepalli, and Alan Fern; NeurIPS 2021, Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 34, pp. 11352–11363; arXiv:2011.06733.
relevance_class: Method-adjacent: image explanation multiplicity and a human counterfactual-understanding study; not forensic authenticity or evidence-correctness research.
scope_and_methods: Full 12-page NeurIPS paper reviewed. Structured Attention Graphs encode multiple minimal sufficient image regions and confidence changes under patch deletion. The main between-subject study recruited 60 university engineering students; each answered 10 comparative questions about which occluded ImageNet subimage would preserve the original class score, with/without SAG, Grad-CAM, or I-GOS. A separate 40-person ablation compared graph and interaction components.
observed_reliability_evidence: In the main study, SAG users averaged 8.6/10 correct (SD 1.698), versus 5.4 (SD 1.188) for I-GOS and 5.3 (SD 1.031) for Grad-CAM; both comparisons were reported p<.0001. SAG users' confidence was better aligned with answer correctness, which is a human model-behavior prediction/calibration signal. The ablation suggests both graph structure and interactive highlighting contributed to task performance.
limitations_and_construct_boundary: The study asks users to predict the classifier's response to synthetic occlusions, not to judge whether an explanation identifies actual forensic evidence or whether an authenticity verdict is correct. It uses ImageNet image classification and a small set of 10 image/question contexts, with university engineering students; confidence alignment is not real-world appropriate reliance. No forensic ground truth, expert forensic raters, explanation-randomization test, or detector explanation faithfulness evaluation is reported.
screening_conclusion: Retain as a useful human-task and explanation-multiplicity neighbor. It supports evaluating whether explanations help users predict model behavior, but cannot establish forensic evidence truth, decision validity, or appropriate reliance in image-authenticity work.
